2 medium potatoes (rounds): 1 small onion (grated)

Knead the mince, grated onion, breadcrumbs, egg, 1 teaspoon salt, cumin and black pepper for 3 minutes; rest in the fridge for 20 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C; toss the potato rounds with olive oil and the remaining salt.
Take walnut-sized pieces of the mixture and shape flat köfte.
Stand the köfte, potato and zucchini rounds upright in turn on the tray; tuck tomato slices and peppers in between.
Dissolve the tomato paste in hot water and drizzle over the tray; cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes.
Remove the foil and bake for 15 more minutes until the köfte are browned.
Potatoes cook more slowly than zucchini, so slice them thin and the zucchini thick.
Serve hot with rice pilaf and yogurt.
Tray-baked köfte with eggplant
3 eggplants (thick rounds)
1 slice stale bread (crumb only)
4 long green peppers
Peel the eggplants in stripes and cut into 2 cm rounds; soak in salted water for 15 minutes and pat dry, toss with 2 tablespoons olive oil and pre-bake at 200 °C for 15 minutes.
Knead the mince, onion, soaked and squeezed bread, egg, salt, cumin and black pepper.
Shape flat köfte about the size of the eggplant rounds.
Stand them upright on the tray, alternating one eggplant and one köfte; tuck tomato slices and peppers in between.
Dissolve the tomato paste in hot water and drizzle over the tray with the remaining olive oil; bake at 200 °C for 25 minutes.
Once browned on top, rest for 5 minutes and serve.
Pre-baking the eggplant gives a lighter result than frying.
Serve hot with rice pilaf.
